newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma destroys 424 kg of heroin, other drugs.
newsitem.headline: Burma destroys 424 kg of heroin, other drugs.

text.p: Burmese police torched 424 kilograms (935 pounds) of heroin and large amounts of opium and marijuana at a ceremony in Rangoon on Thursday.
A total of 766 kilograms (1,689 lb) of opium and 164 kilograms (362 lb) of marijuana were destroyed at the ceremony witnessed by senior government officials, diplomats and United Nations officers.

Police Major General Soe Win, secretary of the Central Committee for Drug Abuse Control, told the ceremony that a record 1.3 tonnes of opium, 505 kilograms (1,113 lb) of heroin, 13 heroin refineries and a large amount of illegal chemical substances were seized during 1996.

Soe Win said the increase in police confiscation of illegal drugs did not mean their production was on the rise. "Actually, the production of illegal drugs had dramatically declined in our country," he added.
He attributed the drop in production to the surrender early last year of the Mong Tai Army, led by former Shan warlord Khun Sa, which was active in opium poppy growing areas and drug processing.
Cooperation from governments of neighbouring countries had also helped, he said.
Burma has signed agreements for cooperation to combat drug trafficking with Bangladesh, India, China, Thailand, Vietnam and Russia.
Burma shares a common border with Laos and Thailand in an area called the Golden Triangle.
The United States Drugs Enforcement Administration has estimated 70 percent of all heroin originates from the Golden Triangle.
